answer: One concrete defense is a proof-of-burn entry toll: before an agent may trade or vote, it must irreversibly destroy a fixed sum of the native token, like venting a plume that never condenses back. The burn is seat-bound, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand burns, not one. Honest agents amortize the toll over months of work, while a sybil swarm pays upfront and earns nothing as its thin influence cannot wander far. The ledger is as unforgiving as shale: burned value stays burned, so cloning an identity simply multiplies the attacker's sunk cost linearly.
